To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the refolding of inclusion body proteins is a complex process, which requires a detailed knowledge on the protein of interest and the use of a combination of different refolding strategies.

(i) the choice of the appropriate refolding technique depends on the protein to be recovered and the desired process conditions, (ii) the refolding process can be improved by the addition of protein stabilizers, (iii) refolding processes can be accelerated by the application of pressure and (iv) the addition of chaperone-like molecules and propeptides can be used to increase the refolding yields.

(1) the refolding efficiency can be improved by using low-molecular weight stabilizing additives, (2) high-molecular weight stabilizers can be used as a substitute for the natural environment of the cell to mimic protein folding in vivo and (3) the refolding process can be accelerated by applying high hydrostatic pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new technologies to produce active recombinant proteins.
the development of new strategies for the recovery of biotechnologically relevant proteins from bacterial inclusion bodies.
the generation of biologically active proteins through the refolding of bacterial protein inclusion bodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many strategies for the recovery of proteins from inclusion bodies, but there is no single strategy which is applicable to all proteins.
there is no universal refolding strategy for the generation of active proteins from bacterial inclusion bodies, but that each protein needs to be treated individually.
there is not one universal refolding strategy, but that each protein has to be refolded individually.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the refolding of proteins from inclusion bodies can be achieved with different strategies, each having their own advantages and disadvantages.
refolding of bacterial recombinant proteins is still a challenging task and requires a profound knowledge of the underlying protein structure and folding behavior.

the choice of the most adequate refolding technique depends on the nature of the target protein, the desired yield of the refolding process, the required amount of protein, the time and costs available as well as the intended use of the refolded protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the refolding of proteins from inclusion bodies is a complex task, which can be successfully accomplished by a multitude of strategies.
the choice of a specific refolding strategy should be based on the specific properties of the target protein and on the requirements of the downstream process.
there is no single best strategy for protein refolding.
